chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAffān, from Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed Allah, Majestic is His praise, apologizes to His believing servant who was made needy in the world, just as a brother apologizes to his brother. So He says: “By My might and My majesty, I did not make you needy in the world because of any abasement of you before Me. So lift this curtain and look at what I have compensated you with in place of the world.”
He عليه السلام said: “So he lifts it and says: ‘What You withheld from me did not harm me, alongside what You compensated me with.’”

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life and its temporary provisions
key_terms.السِّجْفَ: the curtain or veil that is lifted to reveal the reward
key_terms.الْمُحْوِجِ: the one made needy or impoverished in worldly life
key_terms.عَوَّضْتُكَ: I compensated you; divine recompense for worldly deprivation
key_terms.وَجَلَالِي: an oath by Allah’s majesty and grandeur
key_terms.وَعِزَّتِي: an oath by Allah’s might and honor

ai.seo_question: Does poverty in this world mean a believer is dishonored by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that worldly poverty for a believer is not a sign of humiliation before Allah, but may be accompanied by a tremendous divine compensation. It emphasizes Allah’s justice, mercy, and the immense reward awaiting the needy believer in the hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ali Bin Affan, from Mufazzal Bin Umar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allahazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Praise Apologises to Hisazwj Momin servant, the one needy in the world, just as the brother apologises to his brother, so Heazwj Saying: ‘By Myazwj Honour and Myazwj Majesty! Iazwj did not Impoverish you in the world for Humiliation with you. So raise this Curtain and look at what Iazwj have Compensated you from (instead of) the world”.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So he would raise it, and he would be saying, ‘It did not harm me what You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Prevented from me, with You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> have Compensated to me’’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ali ibn ‘Affan from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Allah, the Most Exalted of praise, will apologize to His believing servants who are poor in this world just as a brother apologizes to a brother and He will say, ‘I swear by my Majesty and Glory that I did not make you poor in the world considering you insignificant. Remove this curtain and look what I have given you in exchange for your poverty in the world. ’
The Imam said, ‘He will then raise the curtain and say, ‘(O Lord,) your withholding the wealth of the world from me in exchange for what You have kept in reserve for me has not harmed me at all.”’
